analysis.evidence: וְהָיָה introduces the situation Abram foresees. כִּי יִרְאוּ אֹתָךְ הַמִּצְרִים sets the time, “when the Egyptians see you,” and וְאָמְרוּ introduces what they will say.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes the Qal perfect third-person masculine singular. The resulting weqatal has future reference in Abram’s prediction.

analysis.evidence: After וְהָיָה, כִּי introduces the anticipated event “when the Egyptians see you.” The following וְאָמְרוּ introduces what they will then say.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68619:8, 68613:4, 66585:4, 66577:3, 66561:4, 66324:3.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular construct noun with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.
